cells.tense: You are holding many true things at once right now, and it is not confusing you.
cells.ask: Take the next step that has already shown itself, and when someone asks why, give the plain reason instead of the whole map of it.
cells.core:
You're holding a lot of true things at once, and it isn't confusing you. Nothing in you is demanding they all fit together before you move, which is the whole trick — most people can't do it. When something matters, you tend to say so, and what you say turns out to have weight behind it.

What's working is that not-knowing doesn't stop you. You get enough light for the next step, and you take it, and the step doesn't feel like a guess. There's a cost to carrying this much: the plain reason tends to go missing when you explain yourself. Tell one person the short version, the one that doesn't need the whole picture behind it.
cells.sheetLine: You move without waiting to see the whole road.
cells.verb: holding many true things at once without forcing them into one
cells.place: in the place where the way ahead isn't clear yet

cells.tense: You will have sorted all of this out by the time it arrives, and you are living in that version now.
cells.ask: Pick one of the possibilities you're holding and act on that alone for a day, letting the others wait.
cells.core:
The working version of this is a wide view that still lets you move: several readings in hand, one step taken, and the step lands because it came from more than one angle at once. That's what carrying many things is for. Right now you're out ahead of the moment instead, settling it before it arrives — every angle weighed and compared, and none of them quite landing, because you're standing in a version where they've already been sorted.

Weighing and deciding may have swapped jobs, and that much inspection doesn't stay still long enough to become direction. Pick one possibility and act on it alone, for a day. Let the others wait their turn.
cells.sheetLine: You're settling everything ahead of time, and it's keeping you ahead.
cells.verb: holding many true things at once without forcing them into one

cells.tense: You stopped trusting what you saw in the middle of a situation you were already in.
cells.ask: Say one thing you're unsure about to another person and let them sit with it, before you've worked it out.
cells.core:
You can see a lot from where you stand, and you've stopped saying any of it out loud. Going second has become the way you move in a room — you watch, you let someone else name it first, and what you see stays where no one can check it. That seeing didn't go anywhere. Your hands are in your pockets.

Insight isn't the shortage here; you have plenty. What's off is putting any of it on the table before it's confirmed, and that gets rebuilt in front of someone. Put one uncertain thing in front of another person, before it's worked out. Let the working out happen where someone else can see it, and let that be enough for today.

cells.tense: You are already choosing among the versions, and you're calling the choosing something else.
cells.ask: Name the choice that's already being made — to yourself, out loud, once — instead of letting it look like more study.
cells.core:
You're sifting through several readings of this, and the picking is already underway — when someone else takes a side, you can hear your own lean answer it. You call this keeping options open. The choice is further along than that, and the things you say are fair still get weighed as if they were all tied.

That's not something to fix, only something unclaimed. You'd know what's fair here if you looked at it plainly, and it stays unnamed because looking feels bigger than the moment warrants. Say it once, to yourself, in your own voice: this is the one being picked. The options can stay on the table. You don't have to keep them all even.
cells.sheetLine: You've already picked. You're still calling it open.
